answers.core:
This is about improving the out of the box experience for developing 3D games in Godot, especially games with a pixel art aesthetic.

Newcomers to the engine sometimes don't even know why their textures look worse in Godot, so this provides an automatic solution that is still efficient.[^1] Also, this would benefit anyone using `icon.png` in their 3D projects as it wouldn't be reimported with VRAM compression enabled as soon as you use it in 3D.

[^1]: If there are concerns about it feeling too "magic", note that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/62023 prints a special message when a small texture is detected as used in 3D. This way, the user is aware that such textures are treated differently from others.
answers.workaround: Automatic VRAM compression can be disabled in the Project Settings' Import defaults by setting **Detect 3D > Compress To** to **Disabled**. However, this applies to all textures regardless of their size, so it's not always optimal.

title: Disable VRAM compression by default for small textures in Detect 3D
